score_notes.scripture: NBC-USA generally evangelical-Baptist on Scripture but lacks tight inerrancy confession; local posture varies.
score_notes.gender: NBC-USA varies congregation by congregation; Aker is male senior pastor but NBC-USA broadly permits women pastors.
score_notes.leadership: Male senior pastor; deacons + ministry-leader structure typical of NBC-USA.
score_notes.cultural: NBC-USA churches commonly engage social-justice themes; specific posture at Cornerstone not surveyed.
score_notes.preaching: Black-Baptist homiletic tradition — narrative-driven, not strict expository.
score_notes.mission: Bed-Stuy community engagement; Jeffries himself served as a Cornerstone usher in his youth, suggesting strong intergenerational discipleship.
score_notes.mens_discipleship: Cornerstone's usher culture (Jeffries became "white-gloved, dues-paying usher") indicates institutional formation of young men in service roles.
score_notes.denominational: NBC-USA — largest Black Baptist body; generally conservative on Christology and Scripture but progressive on race/justice; sexuality posture varies.

churches.assessment: Cornerstone Baptist Church at 574 Madison Street in Bedford-Stuyvesant, Brooklyn, is the lifelong home church of House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY-8). Jeffries grew up in Crown Heights and was formed at Cornerstone — in his youth becoming one of the church's white-gloved, dues-paying ushers, tending to crying babies and handling neighborhood traffic during worship. Cornerstone is institutionally part of the National Baptist Convention USA, the largest historically Black Baptist denomination. Rev. Lawrence E. Aker III is current senior pastor. NBC-USA is generally evangelical-Baptist on core doctrine but specific posture on sexuality, women in pastoral ministry, and biblical inerrancy varies by congregation. Per MOOP rubric this is YELLOW — would need on-site verification of confessional posture and pulpit theology before a recommendation; included with notable-attendees context for the most prominent Democratic House leader.
churches.denomination_detail: National Baptist Convention USA — historic Black Baptist congregation in Bed-Stuy.
churches.gender_detail: Male senior pastor (Rev. Lawrence E. Aker III); NBC-USA denominational posture on women clergy varies congregation by congregation.

churches.assessment: Fellowship Missionary Baptist Church Chicago — known affectionately as "the Ship" — was founded September 10, 1950 by Rev. Dr. Clay Evans (1925-2019), the gospel-and-civil-rights legend whose ministry launched the careers of more than 90 ministers, including Rev. Jesse Louis Jackson Sr., who was ordained at Fellowship in 1968. Evans opened the church's doors to Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. during the Chicago Freedom Movement and helped Jackson launch Operation Breadbasket and later Operation PUSH/Rainbow Coalition from this congregation. Evans served as founding National Board Chairman of Rainbow PUSH 1971-1976. Rev. Charles Jenkins succeeded Evans as Senior Pastor after Evans's December 8, 2000 retirement. Listed for civic/political/civil-rights historical significance.

notable_attendees.title: Founder Rainbow PUSH Coalition; Shadow U.S. Senator for D.C. 1991-1997; Democratic presidential candidate 1984 + 1988; civil rights leader; ordained Baptist minister

churches.assessment: Maranatha Baptist Church in Plains, Georgia is the small-town Baptist congregation where President Jimmy Carter taught Sunday school for nearly four decades — from 1981 until his health declined in 2019. The church drew international visitors who came specifically to hear Carter teach; he funeralized there in January 2025. Rev. Tony Lowden was Carter's personal pastor and the first Black lead pastor, succeeded by Rev. Ashley Guthas in 2024 — the church's first woman pastor (a divorced mother of two). In March 2025 under Guthas the church removed American flags from the sanctuary. Maranatha is independent / CBF-aligned (Cooperative Baptist Fellowship, formed 1991 by ex-SBC moderates over biblical-inerrancy and women-in-ministry questions). Carter himself publicly broke with the SBC over its 2000 BFM revision restricting women from senior pastor roles. Per MOOP rubric the female-senior-pastor + CBF-progressive denominational posture is RED on gender / leadership; included for situational awareness about the most famous lay-led Bible-teaching church in America under Carter.
churches.denomination_detail: Independent Baptist; CBF-aligned (Cooperative Baptist Fellowship); broke with SBC trajectory under Carter.
churches.gender_detail: Female senior pastor since 2024 (Rev. Ashley Guthas, first woman pastor in the congregation's history).

Ashley Guthas as senior pastor since 2024 (first woman pastor; divorced mother of two) + Carter's nearly-four-decade Sunday school teaching 1981-2019 + Carter funeral held at Maranatha January 2025 + Tony Lowden as Carter's personal pastor before Guthas + March 2025 sanctuary flag removal under Guthas.

score_notes.christology: Baptist Trinitarian baseline; not the disqualifier here.
score_notes.scripture: Public posture under Brown (and continuing) emphasizes social-gospel and reparations framing over biblical-inerrancy commitments; ABC-USA progressive on sexuality.
score_notes.gender: ABC-USA permits women in pastoral and senior-pastoral roles; egalitarian leadership.
score_notes.leadership: Senior pastor model without complementarian male-eldership posture.
score_notes.soteriology: Baptist baseline but framed primarily through liberation/social-justice lens in public sermons of long-time pastor Brown.
score_notes.cultural: Heavy public emphasis on reparations, racial-justice activism, DNC engagement (Brown gave DNC convention prayer 2024); fits MOOP rubric red for "DEI/CRT language crowding out gospel".
score_notes.mission: Community-organizing + civil-rights advocacy primary; Great Commission language secondary.
score_notes.denominational: ABC-USA — most progressive of major Baptist bodies (American Baptist Churches USA has been broadly affirming-leaning since 1970s).

churches.assessment: Third Baptist Church of San Francisco is the oldest African-American Baptist congregation west of the Rockies (founded 1852). For nearly half a century — 1976 to 2025 — it was pastored by Rev. Amos C. Brown, a civil-rights leader and close advisor to Kamala Harris. Brown gave the convention prayer at the 2024 DNC. Harris has been a member for more than 20 years and worked for Brown's campaign for San Francisco supervisor in 2000; he was reportedly among the first people she called when Joe Biden suspended his 2024 campaign and she became the presumptive Democratic nominee. Rev. Devon Jerome Crawford succeeded Brown on July 1, 2025. Theologically the congregation operates in the progressive Black social-gospel tradition with heavy reparations and racial-justice framing; ABC-USA affiliation places it on the affirming end of Baptist polity. Per MOOP rubric this is RED; included for situational awareness about the home church of a recent Democratic nominee for President.
churches.denomination_detail: American Baptist Churches USA (ABC-USA) + National Baptist Convention USA dual affiliation; historic Black Baptist congregation founded 1852.
churches.gender_detail: Egalitarian — ABC-USA permits women pastors and elders.
churches.enrichment_notes: Live-fetched Wikipedia + Sojourners + Christian Post + Baptist Standard + Christian Century coverage on 2026-05-16 — confirmed Rev. Devon Jerome Crawford as senior pastor since 2025-07-01 (succeeded Rev. Amos C. Brown 1976-2025) + 1399 McAllister St + founded 1852 + Kamala Harris longtime member. Note: previous MOOP directory entry for "third-baptist-louisville" had broken URL pointing to thirdbaptist.org (this San Francisco congregation) — separate church; Louisville is thirdavenue.org.

score_notes.denominational: 1689 LBCF Reformed Baptist confessional adherence stated on church website.

churches.assessment: President Warren G. Harding joined the Free Baptist Church in Marion on May 6, 1883, served as a trustee for 25 years and as a deacon, and remained a member until his death in 1923. The Free Baptist Church merged with the First Baptist Church via a joint worship service on September 24, 1911, and was renamed Trinity Baptist Church in April 1912. The congregation that today carries Harding's historical pew has, in the contemporary era, embraced a robust 1689 London Baptist Confession Reformed Baptist confessional identity under Pastor Daniel McCoy (DTS / Master's Seminary), with explicit 9Marks and Founders Ministries affiliation. Worth noting: Harding personally was a theologically liberal Baptist (per Patheos historical assessment), so the present-day Trinity Baptist is more confessionally robust than the congregation Harding inhabited.

notable_attendees.name: President Warren G. Harding
notable_attendees.title: 29th President of the United States 1921-1923; U.S. Senator (R-OH) 1915-1921; Lt. Gov. of Ohio 1904-1906
notable_attendees.source_title: Patheos / Anxious Bench (Daniel Williams): "President Warren Harding's Liberal Baptist Faith" — Harding joined Free Baptist Marion 1883; served as trustee 25 years and deacon; membership maintained until death; Free Baptist + First Baptist merged into Trinity Baptist 1912

churches.enrichment_notes: Live-fetched https://tbcmarion.org/ on 2026-05-16 — confirmed Pastor Daniel McCoy and 1689 LBCF / 9Marks / Founders Ministries confessional posture (NOTE: task prompt assumed SBC; live website states Independent Baptist with explicit confessional affiliations — corrected to Independent Baptist 1689 LBCF). Founding history of the present Trinity Baptist (1911 merger / 1912 rename) per tbcmarion.org/our-story and Library of Congress photo archive ggbain.30659. Harding deacon/trustee tenure documented in Patheos historical assessment by Daniel Williams.

Treat directory presence as a self-attested signal of alignment with the 9 Marks values; confirm independently before publishing.
churches.gender_detail: Verify on church website — 9Marks Church-Search listings self-attest to complementarian polity but the directory does not enforce.
churches.denomination_detail: 9Marks Church-Search listing — a self-submitted directory of churches affirming the 9 Marks of a Healthy Church (Dever): expositional preaching, biblical theology, biblical gospel, conversion, evangelism, membership, church discipline, discipleship, and elder-led leadership. Inclusion is user-submitted via a public form, NOT vetted by 9Marks editorial staff.
